requirements.title: List-directed records are values and separators with record-end and blank normalization
requirements.definition: List-directed records form a sequence of values and value separators; outside character constants, end of record acts as a blank and two or more consecutive blanks act as one blank.

pending.record-end-as-blank: Internal READ from two character records ['1','2'] into two integers with list-directed input; exact records are '1' and '2', expected values are 1 and 2 because the first record end separates values as a blank.
pending.multiple-blanks-collapse: Internal READ from record '1   2' into two integers; expected values are 1 and 2, proving a run of blanks is one separator, not zeros or null values.
pending.character-constants-preserve-blanks: Internal READ record "'A  B'" into character(len=4); expected value is exactly 'A  B', preserving the two embedded blanks inside the character constant.

requirements.title: List-directed input values have null, constant, repeated-constant, and repeated-null forms
requirements.definition: A value is a null value, c, r*c, or r*; c and r have no kind type parameters; c is interpreted with the kind of the corresponding effective item; repeated forms are equivalent to successive constants or nulls and contain no embedded blanks except inside c where permitted.

pending.constant-value: Internal READ record '17' into default integer; expected value 17.
pending.repeat-constant: Internal READ record '3*5' into integer array(3); expected values [5,5,5].
pending.repeat-null: Initialize integer array to [1,2,3], internal READ record '2*' into first two elements; expected values remain [1,2,3] for those null effective items.
pending.no-kind-parameters: Deferred negative: record '1_4' as a list-directed integer value differs from the control '1' only by a kind type parameter in c; observe only a required input-error condition if the future Clause 12 owner supplies portable IOSTAT mechanics, not a compile-time diagnostic.
pending.no-embedded-blanks-in-repeat-form: Deferred negative: record '2 *5' differs from '2*5' only by an embedded blank in the r*c form; future fixture must isolate that input-error property.

requirements.title: List-directed value separators are comma or semicolon, slash, or qualifying blanks
requirements.definition: A value separator is the comma form (or semicolon in COMMA decimal edit mode), the slash form, or one or more blanks between nonblank values or after the last nonblank value.

pending.comma-separator: Internal READ record '1, 2' into two integers; expected values 1 and 2.

pending.slash-separator: Internal READ record '1 / 99' into integer variables initialized to -1; expected first value 1 and following effective item unchanged through null-supply semantics owned by 13.10.3.2 p3.
pending.blank-separator: Internal READ record '1 2 ' into two integers; expected values 1 and 2.

review_rationale: Independent fresh-context source review, two rounds: doc/source_audits/batch_139.json. This COMPLETES the list-directed and namelist half of Clause 13. The reviewer re-derived unit hashes, re-partitioned the four sections sharing PDF p312 unit by unit, verified the zero-numbered-R/C claim across all 77 units, re-read both note result tables row-by-row (13.10.3.2 NOTE 3 and 13.11.3.6 NOTE), and confirmed 13.10.4 contains no table despite being the flagged candidate. THE CRUX of this scope is the REQUIRED versus PROCESSOR-DEPENDENT split, and the reviewer audited it in BOTH directions, producing two blocking findings that are the same error in mirror image. C139SR-001: the F/E choice for real list-directed output was marked WHOLLY processor-dependent, but 13.10.4 p5 fixes one case - a real ZERO must use F form - so the claim was TOO BROAD, which is itself a defect; the unit is now split, with a required facet asserting ONLY the form (no E-form exponent marker) and explicitly not the width, digits, sign or decimal spelling, and 13.11.4.2 propagating it through namelist editing. C139SR-002 ran the other way: a plan asserted the exact substring I= while the same packet marked spacing around equals processor-dependent, and a conforming processor may emit I with a space; the plan now asserts the uppercase object-name token only. The genuine obligations survive and were hand-verified including their leading blanks: ' T' and ' F' from 13.10.4 p3 with p13, ' AB' for delimiter mode NONE from p8, and the namelist prefix ' &G' from 13.11.4.3 p3 and p5. Source accounting only: authored_facets unchanged at 1977, no fixture bound, no compiler invoked.
